title: Colouring bijections of finite $3$-groups
summary: Let $G$ be a finite group. A bijection $σ\colon G\to G$ is a \emph{colouring bijection} if the three maps \[ Δ^{+}\colon x\mapsto x\,σ(x), \qquad Δ^{-}\colon x\mapsto x^{-1}σ(x), \qquad Δ^{c}\colon x\mapsto σ(x)^{-1}x\,σ(x) \] are again bijections of $G$. The first two conditions say that $σ$ is a strong complete mapping. The third is a genuinely nonabelian requirement. Our main theorem is that every noncyclic $3$-group not isomorphic to the modular group $M_{3^{r}}$ $(r\ge4)$ admits a colouring bijection.
